key_insight: The paper replaces the usual special-quasirandom-structure plus ideal-entropy approximation with a cumulant expansion of free energy that captures short-range order in disordered phases.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more accurate screening of finite-temperature phase stability, defect populations, and order–disorder behavior for alloys and ionic materials without expensive Monte Carlo or molecular dynamics.
method: Treat free energy as an expansion in energy cumulants rather than a single SQS energy plus ideal entropy.
Estimate higher-order cumulants directly from energies of random atomic arrangements.
Use the resulting model to predict phase diagrams, defect concentrations, and short-range order, and to screen Li-excess rocksalt oxides across 26 elements.
evidence_signal: In a nine-element refractory system, including the second cumulant reduced free-energy errors by about an order of magnitude, and the approach was used to identify synthesizable Li-excess rocksalt oxides rich in Li4 clusters.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on how well random-configuration energy sampling captures the relevant cumulants, and the expansion may be less reliable if strong correlations or sampling gaps are present.
paper_title: Beyond special quasirandom structures: free energies from energy cumulants
